findings.citation: spec.md:325 "| `NUMBER_TOO_LONG` | "A SIM number can be at most 64 characters." |"

findings.citation: spec.md:527 "(during implementation) The correction "Edit" buttons carry accessible names per field ("Edit owner", "Edit plan", …) so they stay distinct inside one row."
findings.note: Model and number Edit buttons (also sim-card-number-control.tsx:74) are plain "Edit"; on the Manager's Smartphone row the model Edit and serial Edit share one name.

findings.citation: spec.md:239-240 "Bean Validation on the request DTOs checks presence."
findings.note: None of the four correction DTOs has a constraint and none is @Valid; presence is checked in the services (unlisted OWNER_INVALID; missing plan id -> PLAN_NOT_ON_CARRIER). Same root as F5.

findings.citation: docs/agents/coding-standards.md Backend 1: "Controllers validate the request DTO with `@Valid` + Bean Validation annotations; a service method never re-validates what the controller boundary already checked."
findings.note: No @Valid / Bean Validation on the four correction endpoints (SimCardController.java:181,198; SmartphoneController.java:184,201); services check presence (SimCardCorrectionService.java:94, SmartphoneCorrectionService.java:52,88). Coded 400s must survive (map MethodArgumentNotValidException in the per-controller handler).

findings.citation: docs/agents/coding-standards.md Backend 12: "Table-driven tests (`@ParameterizedTest` + `@MethodSource`) for any method with more than two branch conditions, instead of copy-pasted per-case tests."
findings.note: correctPostpaidPlan refusals are four copy-pasted request/expect blocks (422-446); correctNumber blank/missing/length likewise (166-191).

findings.citation: docs/agents/frontend.md: "A screenshot golden updated on its own, with no code change behind it, is drift" / "updated in the same commit as the code change that moved them"
findings.note: 0fb79bf changes only the 8 Fleet goldens; the code that moved them is 2cd9b6a. History is pushed: do not rewrite; name the code change behind them (as e14310d did on real-manager-dashboard), and any recapture in this fix pass goes in the same commit as its code.

findings.citation: DESIGN.md Layout: "Tables scroll horizontally on narrow viewports (`min-w-[720px]` inside an `overflow-x-auto` wrapper) rather than reflowing to cards."
findings.note: On mobile the SIM number wraps to three lines ("+1-" / "555-" / "0201") beside Edit; same for model (smartphone-model-control.tsx:73) and plan name (sim-card-plan-control.tsx:89). Add whitespace-nowrap to the display value; recapture mobile goldens in the same commit.

findings.citation: PRODUCT.md Accessibility: "Reasonable defaults for an internal operations tool: keyboard operability, sufficient contrast, visible focus states."
findings.note: Edit names don't say which unit: "Edit owner"/"Edit plan" repeat on every row, model/number are bare "Edit" (see F3). Keep visible "Edit"; accessible names with the unit, e.g. "Edit model, {model}", "Edit number, {number}", "Edit owner of {model}", "Edit plan for {number}"; update e2e locators.

findings.citation: PRODUCT.md: "keyboard operability"; DESIGN.md "The Menu Returns Focus Rule … always returns focus to its trigger when it closes" (same open/close shape)
findings.note: All four controls drop focus to <body> on Save/Cancel, and Escape does nothing. Return focus to the Edit button on close; Escape = Cancel; one shared place (e.g. a useInlineEdit hook).
Model and number errors are bare spans (also sim-card-number-control.tsx:100); owner/plan use role="alert" and max-w-56. Give both role="alert", max-w-56, and aria-describedby from the input.

findings.citation: DESIGN.md "The Tabular Everywhere Rule. Every monetary or numeric value … carries `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` via the shared `.tnum` utility — no exceptions"
findings.note: The number Input lacks tnum while the display span has it.

findings.citation: DESIGN.md "The Reserved Indigo Rule. … never as a decorative fill, header rule, or secondary accent. Its rarity is the point…"
findings.note: 12 indigo Edit chips on the Manager Contract golden, 9 on the Tester's, in ragged positions; they outweigh status badges. Switch correction buttons to the ghost variant (28px, always visible) or show full strength only on row hover/focus-within.

findings.citation: DESIGN.md "The Pill-Is-Primary Rule. … A screen with two pill buttons is a defect, not a variant."
findings.note: Pre-existing: "Add smartphone" and "Add SIM card" are both primary pills. Not this feature's lines -> debt. human (2026-10-14): pre-existing; recorded as debt, not fixed here.

findings.citation: DESIGN.md "The Reserved Indigo Rule. … never as a decorative fill … or secondary accent. Its rarity is the point"
findings.note: After F19 the Manager row shows ghost Edit for model and owner but the pre-existing serial control keeps a soft-indigo row "Edit" chip with a bare accessible name. Fix: serial Edit to ghost with aria-label "Edit serial, {serial}"; recapture Manager Contract Fleet goldens in the same commit. human (2026-10-14): recorded as debt, merge without fixing.

The correction MethodArgumentNotValidException handlers (SimCardController.java:215, SmartphoneController.java:225) also catch the controllers' older @Valid endpoints (create, status, serial, installed-in) and return a ProblemDetail body instead of Boot's /error JSON. Also raised by reviewer-spec. No frontend screen reads those bodies (checked create dialogs, serial, installed-in, status controls).
